text:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression in nightly after the recent kernel-selection tweak. p99 decode latency +12% on replay traces. quick profiler snippet below.

priya: ugh, which tweak? the fallback ordering? KV cache changes?

alex: changed fallback to prefer fp16_fused_attention for short contexts, hoping for throughput wins. profiler shows extra memcpy at batch formation step and higher KV write churn. snippet of the batcher config I ran: 
```
batcher.queue_policy = 'age_priority'
batcher.token_budget = 2048
batcher.bucket_boundaries = [0, 32, 128, 512]
```

marco: Are you doing mixed-length batches? when we merge very short + long prompts we end up padding a lot and rewriting KV pages more often.

alex: yes mixed lengths + high token_budget. measurables: KV writes per-batch +3x, avg batch pad ratio 0.46, decode-rate bucket <=50 toks/s dominating p99.

sara: propose experiment: 1) enforce prompt-length buckets before batching, 2) add decode-rate buckets inside each length bucket, 3) soft cap token_budget to 1024, and 4) change queue policy to prefer size_then_age. Keep kernel bias = 'latency' for short buckets.

priya: agreed. also add a slow-decode detection flag to avoid mixing slow decoders with fast ones in same batch. small change but huge latency impact.

alex: setting up a 2-hr perf replay with: 
```
batcher.queue_policy = 'size_then_age'
batcher.token_budget = 1024
batcher.soft_grouping_window_ms = 50
kernel_selection.bias = 'latency'
```
@ci-bot can you enqueue perf-replay/1764123456?

ci-bot: scheduled perf-replay/1764123456: queued -> running (replay against 2026-03-16 traces)

marco: also add a metric: kv_writes_per_request and kv_writes_per_batch histogram on the batcher dashboard. will help correlate.

alex: will add dashboard panels and post results here. initial dry-run shows p99 improvement ~6% and KV writes down ~45%. will report after full replay.

priya: awesome. if numbers hold we should land the queue_policy + token_budget change and revert the fp16_fallback bias until we can optimize memcpy paths. :thumbsup:
